messages:
deploybot: Attempting deploy -> environment: production (canary). Commit: 7a9f3b2 | tag: v3.4.1
deploybot: STATUS: BLOCKED by CI gate. Failing checks: integration-tests (2/5), e2e-flaky-check (1/1). Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/build/4589
ci-bot: Failing jobs:
- integration-tests: test_schema_mismatch (failed)
- integration-tests: test_stream_reconnect (failed)
- e2e-flaky-check: retry limit reached
ci-bot: Full log excerpt:
```
AssertionError: expected 200 but got 502
at tests/integration/test_schema.py:42
```
sara: ack — thanks for the ping. Is this the same schema flake we saw last week?
alexa: looks similar to the schema flake but different stacktrace. last week was a protobuf decode error, this is 502 from our proxy route.
mike: 502 could be regression in canary service or infra throttling. Any recent network changes in this commit? Commit 7a9f3b2 touches routing and batching.
jordan: tagging the owner: @mike can you confirm if routing changes are safe for canary?
mike: checking now. quick grep shows a change to max_concurrent_requests in runtime config. Might be related.
sara: options: 1) manual-unblock and proceed (requires release lead + SRE approval), 2) pin to previous stable tag v3.4.0 and abort canary, 3) abort and rollback deployment entirely. Thoughts?
jordan: +1 for pin and rerun integration tests on a branch build. Safer than forcing forward.
alexa: agree. the failing tests are infra-adjacent; pin avoids risk to users during change window.
mike: if we pin, we should also open a quick postmortem to track whether the change caused regression. I can run a targeted repro against 7a9f3b2 locally.
sara: re: manual unblock — policy requires both release lead and oncall SRE to sign off for infra-impacting failures. neither has signed yet.
deploybot: Manual approval path: use `/deploy override --reason "CI gate - infra 502s" --approvers sara,jordan` (approvals will be recorded).
ci-bot: Rerun hints: you can rerun only failing jobs: `/ci rerun integration-tests --build 4589 --jobs test_schema_mismatch,test_stream_reconnect`
mike: I'll try a local repro and then rerun the failing jobs. If rerun passes, we can consider proceeding with caution (partial canary).
sara: timeline: if we pin -> abort canary now and redeploy v3.4.0 within 10m. If we rerun and all green -> maybe allow canary to continue but limit traffic to 5%.
jordan: note: analytics team will need heads up if we keep canary but limit traffic. They route a/b buckets.
alexa: also add a smoke check for the proxy route during canary to catch 502s early.
mike: local repro started, logs indicate connection pool exhaustion in runtime when concurrent requests spike. Might be the config tweak.
sara: decision: pin to v3.4.0 and schedule a controlled reattempt of v3.4.1 after fix. Proceeding to abort canary now. @deploybot please rollback canary and redeploy tag v3.4.0 to prod canary slot.
deploybot: Acknowledged. Initiating rollback -> target tag: v3.4.0. ETA ~ 6m. 
sara: assigning actions:
- mike: root cause + fix PR (owner)
- alexa: reproduce flaky vs real (qa)
- jordan: verify rollback completed and monitoring (sre)
- sara: coordinate release notes and schedule reattempt
mike: will open PR referencing this thread and include failing job artifacts.
jordan: monitoring hooks added to canary dashboard, alert thresholds lowered temporarily.
deploybot: Rollback complete. Deployed v3.4.0 to prod canary.
sara: thanks all. I'll create an incident/retro doc and add the failing test artifacts. If anyone finds the 502 repro info post-rollback ping here. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Build 4589 marked FAILED. Reruns pending per request.
